title: The 1950s band's sidemen and which band was the best
summary: He names Fontana, Urso, Perkins, Mettome and Fagerquist, and says each band had something to say.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You had some great guys in that band -- Carl Fontana --
That was a whole different grouping again.
Yeah. Did you have Phil Urso, too?

For a short period, yeah. That was the band that once again, Perkins and a lot of different guys. And Doug Mettome, marvelous trumpet player and a young man that -- from Minnesota, another great trumpet player, it's a Nordic name and I can't think of it. Don Fagerquist.

Marvelous player. So it's hard to -- so, like, when people say to me, 'What was your best band,' this was a very difficult question in my case, because I think each one of those bands had something to say, and I think we did it the best we could with what we had to offer, and I think it was great for the time. And that's my only argument, and that's not a cri-

tique as far as Nat or anyone else, who tries to dwell where it was. I have a thing now I say at the end of certain tunes we do, "and that's the way it was." That we should distinguish it from -- that's not the way it is.
